name: Lion's Mane: dense white heads
summary: Cooler fruiting, shade, and steady fresh air for tight, heavy heads with short spines. Cut early for a crab-like texture.
notes: Cut the head when it is firm and the spines are still short, before they lengthen. Cooler rooms can give a faint pink blush; it is harmless. If you see branching coral shapes, the air is too stale.
chamber_notes: Keep the block upright with one opening so you get one big head instead of many small ones. Chamber limits: there is no heater or cooler, so temperature targets only hold if the room sits near them. There is no CO2 sensor, so the fan schedule stands in for fresh air. The humidifier can only add moisture, so a low humidity target depends on dry room air.

source_notes.title: The Mushroom Magazine 2022 lion's mane factory
source_notes.detail: Inside the Factory: Lion's Mane, The Mushroom Magazine, Feb 2022. Fruiting runs 14 to 25 °C with 16 to 18 °C as the ideal. Cooler rooms give denser heads, warmer rooms looser heads with longer spines. CO2 above 0.1% gives coral-like branching. Fruits grow best in shade. Heads are cut 7 to 12 days after they appear, before the spines lengthen.

source_notes.title: Stamets
source_notes.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms (commonly cited chamber ranges). H. erinaceus colonizes ~21 to 24 °C and fruits cooler, often 16 to 20 °C.

stages.name: Pinning
stages.notes: Shade and cool air. One cluster per opening.

stages.name: Fruiting
stages.notes: Cut 7 to 12 days after the head appears, before the spines lengthen.

light_recipe.why: Dim light because the source says lion's mane grows best in shade. 10% white is about 46 lux. Blue stays at the free card level.
light_recipe.wavelength_note: WS2812 red is roughly 620 to 630 nm and blue roughly 465 to 475 nm. The RGB mix is an approximation of the cited wavelengths, not a measured spectrum. RGB percent is LED drive level, not a photon ratio.

sources.title: Jozifek et al. 2025
sources.detail: Miroslav Jozifek et al., Selenium Uptake by Hericium erinaceus Basidiocarps, Agriculture 15 (2025). The main cultivation used 500 lux for 24 h continuous light and caused pink stress coloring. Additional tests at 200 lux or lower on a 12 h cycle produced white basidiocarps. This recipe uses that 200 lux, 12 h schedule. 200 lux maps to 26% white.

sources.title: Sakamoto 2018
sources.detail: Yuichi Sakamoto, Influences of environmental factors on fruiting body induction, development and maturation in mushroom-forming fungi, Fungal Biology Reviews 32 (2018). Light is a fruiting cue for many basidiomycetes. Blue light is the usual photomorphogenesis signal. Agaricus bisporus is called out as not needing light for a cap. Flammulina velutipes can fruit in the dark as a long stem with a tiny cap.
